social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 8 pack-years, quit 5 years ago

patient.chief_complaint: Worst headache of her life while working out, now 6 hours ago, partially improved
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Edwards is a 47-year-old woman with a brother who has an unruptured aneurysm who presents 6 hours after a sudden onset severe headache during a workout at the gym. She was doing jumping jacks when she developed a thunderclap headache rated 10/10, with immediate nausea and vomiting. She sat down, called her husband, and waited to see if it improved. Over 6 hours, the headache improved to 6/10. She has residual neck stiffness and photophobia. Her husband drove her to the ED 6 hours after onset. She initially attributed it to an unusual migraine but notes this headache was instantaneous and more severe than any previous migraine. Given her brother's aneurysm history, she is very concerned. A CT was performed on arrival. She has no focal deficits, no loss of consciousness. Family history of aneurysm significantly elevates her pre-test probability.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; photophobic; mild residual headache 6/10
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 3mm; EOM intact; no papilledema; no CN deficit
neurological_exam.additional: Moderate nuchal rigidity; Kernig positive; Brudzinski equivocal; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.description: Thin bilateral Sylvian fissure blood - subtle at 6 hours from onset

additional_observations: CT sensitivity still approximately 93% at 6 hours
ct.impression: Subtle subarachnoid hemorrhage in bilateral Sylvian fissures and suprasellar cistern (Fisher grade 2). Sensitivity at 6 hours is approximately 93% - LP still required to definitively exclude or confirm SAH. CTA urgently needed.
recommended_actions: LP if SAH clinically suspected despite CT

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 12.4 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 132 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.14 ng/mL (H), BNP 156 pg/mL (H).

ecg.interpretation: Neurogenic T-wave changes. QTc mildly prolonged. Monitor.

findings.finding: Saccular aneurysm 5.6 x 4.8 mm with irregular lobulation - likely ruptured

output.impression: Right MCA aneurysm 5.6 mm consistent with ruptured aneurysm given family history and bilateral Sylvian blood. DSA for treatment.
recommended_actions: Screen first-degree relatives (brother already has known unruptured aneurysm)

output.impression: Mild neurogenic Takotsubo with EF 50%. Monitor. Expected recovery.

findings.status: Moderate vasospasm - right MCA ipsilateral to aneurysm

output.impression: Moderate right MCA vasospasm consistent with right MCA aneurysm. Patient symptomatic with mild right arm weakness. Intensify therapy.

output.query: Familial cerebral aneurysm screening first degree relatives MRA

results.finding: First-degree relative with aneurysm: 3-5x increased risk; 4% prevalence
AHA/ASA: MRA screening recommended for first-degree relatives especially with ≥2 affected family members
Patient has brother with aneurysm - confirmed familial pattern now with her own SAH

output.summary: Confirmed familial aneurysm pattern (brother + patient). All first-degree relatives should receive MRA screening. Family genetic counseling recommended.

findings.description: Reduced CBF 28 mL/100g/min right MCA territory

output.impression: Right MCA territory perfusion compromise with approaching infarction threshold. Urgent intervention required - intra-arterial therapy consideration.
recommended_actions: Intra-arterial verapamil or balloon angioplasty urgently

interactions: Propranolol + nimodipine: additive bradycardia and negative inotropy - significant interaction
warnings: Hold propranolol during nimodipine course in SAH
Monitor HR - propranolol + nimodipine can cause significant bradycardia
Valsartan also adds hypotensive risk - hold during SAH acute phase

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from right MCA bifurcation aneurysm with familial history (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 2)

differential.key_features: CSF bloody with xanthochromia; thunderclap onset; family history of aneurysm
CTA shows saccular aneurysm; CSF confirms SAH

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Subtle bilateral Sylvian SAH at 6 hours
Confirmed familial pattern - screen all first-degree relatives

critical_actions: LP confirms SAH despite partially improving headache
CTA for aneurysm identification - familial history increases index of suspicion
Hold propranolol - significant interaction with nimodipine
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute to migraine without LP
Do not continue propranolol with nimodipine without monitoring for bradycardia
Do not delay aneurysm treatment given familial SAH risk
key_reasoning_points: Familial aneurysm history (brother with unruptured aneurysm) increases pre-test probability significantly
CT at 6 hours showing subtle SAH still requires LP confirmation - 93% sensitivity means ~7% false negative rate
Propranolol + nimodipine: additive calcium/beta blockade causing significant bradycardia risk - hold propranolol
Valsartan (ARB) should also be held during acute SAH phase to prevent hypotension
Day 6 moderate vasospasm ipsilateral to aneurysm demonstrates importance of TCD monitoring
Confirmed familial SAH pattern: patient + brother = recommend first-degree relative screening
